ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against: (i) the current consolidated UN Security Council Sanctions List; (ii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN Lists; (iii) European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) Her Majesty's Treasury Consolidated List of Financial Sanctions Targets; and (v) the Central Bank of Samoa's AML/CFT directives and local criminal records. Must include automated and manual negative-news checks for exposure as Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined under Section 2 of the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, including immediate family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence applies to any PEP, with senior management approval required and ongoing transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) Company Registry – Online Name Reservation and Clearance Portal: https://www.sifa.gov.ws/company-registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in English characters (Latin alphabet). A proposed name may additionally include Samoan or Chinese script provided that an English transliteration or translation is submitted with the registration application. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing Samoan international company, a domestic company, or a reserved name. For Chinese character names, an exact romanized or English-equivalent rendering must be certified by a qualified translator. Any name appearing in a foreign script will be recorded in the registry with the English representation only, and the Chinese character version will be held as an auxiliary translation. The statutory language of the Certificate of Name Reservation and the Certificate of Incorporation remains English.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: or any abbreviation thereof where the Registrar deems it would suggest a different corporate form or regulated activity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its licensed registered agent must file a formal written appeal to the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days from the date of rejection notice. The appeal letter must state the grounds upon which the proposed name should be accepted or distinguished from the objecting or conflicting mark, provide supporting documentation (e.g., prior registration certificates, letters of consent, trademark registrations), and pay the prescribed administrative appeal fee (USD 200). The Registrar must issue a written determination within 21 working days. If the Registrar rejects the appeal, the applicant may file an application to the Supreme Court of Samoa for judicial review under the Judgment Act 1961. Name reservations may be extended for a further 30-day period on payment of the extension fee, but no single extension may extend the reservation beyond 90 days from the initial approval date.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted with limitations. A virtual office is permissible for administrative purposes only, provided that the company maintains a physical registered office in Samoa at the office of a licensed registered agent. The registered office must be staffed during normal business hours and be capable of receiving service of process and official correspondence. For a low-risk independent film licensing company, virtual access to directors and remote management portals is acceptable, but the physical site of the registered agent must remain the legal domicile of the company. No mail-forwarding only arrangement will satisfy the statutory mandate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-zero. Based on the risk tier 'Low_Risk_Standard' and the absence of a statutory license, the estimated likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Samoa International Financial Authority within the first twelve months of operation is 10%. The likelihood increases to 25% if the company applies for a banking relationship with a Samoan financial institution or if any adverse AML/CFT indicator is triggered.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (No. 28 of 1987) as amended — ss. 7 (Application and Certificate of Incorporation), 9 (Registered Office), 10 (Registered Agent), 11 (Memorandum of Association), 16 (Shares); read with the International Companies Regulations 1991.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International and Foreign Companies, Companies and International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Prescribed Application for Incorporation of an International Company submitted under s. 7 of the International Companies Act 1987, together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the International Companies Act 1987, s. 16; shares may be issued at nominal value, and no escrow or capital deposit account is required for an International Company. A higher registration fee may apply where authorized capital exceeds US$100,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Unanimous resolution of the sole incorporator and founding shareholder adopting: (1) the subscription and allotment of 100 fully paid ordinary shares for US$1.00 each to the founding member, entered in the register of members; (2) the registered office at the licensed registered agent's address in Apia, Samoa, under Section 9 of the International Companies Act 1987; (3) the appointment of [Director Name] as Director and [Secretary Name] as Secretary, each to serve until removed by resolution; and (4) authorization for officers and the registered agent to open bank accounts, affix the common seal, and execute all filing matters as may be necessary to obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia; submissions made through the licensed registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request proposing up to three names ending in 'Limited' or 'Ltd' for the International Company. The Registrar checks the Register for prohibited, undesirable or confusingly similar names and, if approved, reserves the preferred name for 28 days pending incorporation. Retain the written clearance for use in the Memorandum and Articles.
required_dossiers: Three preferred company names in priority order
Certified passport copy of the founding shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused, the registered agent may file written representations within 7 days or select the next preferred name; a fresh application may be made with a modified name, and administrative re-submission is available under the International Companies Act 1987.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent approved by the Registrar, assisted by a notary public in Samoa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, stating the company name, authorized share capital, share structure, registered office address and permitted international objects. The founding subscriber executes both documents before a notary public, completing the subscription particulars, date and signature; two original counterparts are prepared for filing and for the company records.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Passport and proof-of-address copies of subscriber(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies are cured by re-execution of corrected drafts before the same notary; if statutory content is missing, the Registrar issues a requisition allowing a defined period for filing conforming documents prior to refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Application for Incorporation and Payment of State Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International and Foreign Companies, MCIL Companies Registry, Apia (counter lodgement or via licensed registered agent).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the prescribed Application for Incorporation together with the executed Memorandum and Articles, the registered agent's consent, consents of each proposed director and secretary, and proof of payment of the official state fee. The registered office address in Samoa must be stated in the application. Retain the date-stamped acknowledgment for tracking and completion of the statutory scrutiny process.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (two sets)
Consent to act as registered agent
Consents of the first director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query, the registered agent files an explanatory response and any amended documents within 10 business days; if the application is refused, a fresh application is made once the stated ground of refusal is cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Opening of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International and Foreign Companies (certificate issuance); directors and registered agent (corporate records).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following successful scrutiny, the Registrar assigns a company number, enters the company in the Register of International Companies and issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The registered agent collects the Certificate and delivers the original to the company; the directors then open the register of members, register of directors and secretaries, issue share certificates and prepare the common seal.
required_dossiers: Share certificates and common seal specimen
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Errors in the Certificate are rectified by an application supported by the Certificate and a statutory declaration; errors in allotment records are corrected by board resolution and amendment of the register in accordance with the International Companies Act 1987.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of the First Board Resolution and Post-Incorporation Governance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the International Company; licensed registered agent; correspondent bank for account opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass the unanimous written First Board Resolution to allot the founding shares, fix the registered office, appoint the first director and secretary, authorise the opening of bank accounts and the affixing of the common seal. File the resolution in the corporate minute book, deliver certified copies to the registered agent and the bank, and complete the AML/KYC file for account opening.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution (original or certified copy)
AML/KYC banking pack (passports, proof of address, corporate chart)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resolution is defective, a ratifying board resolution is adopted; any change in the registered office or officers is filed using the prescribed notification form within the statutory time limit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial establishment. For a physical administrative office in Samoa, the Trade and Industry Division, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) administers general business licensing matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — an International Company formed under the International Companies Act 1987 may carry on film-copyright international distribution and licensing activities directly upon incorporation, without an operating or manufacturing licence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) / Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), administering the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-only international company; no full EIA report or Development Consent is triggered by incorporation for motion-picture copyright distribution and licensing, as no construction, manufacturing or land disturbance occurs. PUMA screening applies only if a physical development or industrial operation is later established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no process wastewater, VOC emissions or hazardous waste streams are generated by copyright licensing activities; office waste is disposed through Apia municipal solid waste services, and any future physical operations would require prior PUMA environmental screening and compliance with Samoa's environmental discharge standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the registered office business suite issued by the Samoa Fire & Emergency Services Authority (FESA), covering smoke detection, extinguishers and egress; structural load inspection is not required for non-industrial office occupancy but building occupancy clearances apply; workplace and occupational safety compliance is administered under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013 by the Labour Division, MCIL.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Ministry of Revenue; online taxpayer portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an International Company (IC): (1) incorporate under the International Companies Act 1987 via the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); (2) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and statutory company records; (3) if the IC makes taxable supplies connected to Samoa (i.e., domestic annual turnover equal or exceeding WST 60,000) or elects voluntary registration, submit the SRA taxpayer/VAGST registration application (Form VAGST-01 / SRA Online taxpayer registration) with certified charter, incorporation certificate, director and shareholder details, and the Samoa registered office address; (4) SRA issues a TIN/VAGST number upon approval. ICs whose supplies are exclusively offshore are exempt from income tax and are not required to hold a VAGST TIN unless they make local taxable supplies; voluntary registration is available to recover input credits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — International Company is exempt from income tax and most local levies under the International Companies Act 1987 (Part XVII); territorial scope limits taxation to Samoa-source economic activity; no capital gains tax and no withholding tax on distributions to non-resident shareholders.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or US-style entity classification election exists in Samoa; the IC tax exemption is automatic and non-elective. No hybrid mismatch election is available as Samoa has not adopted BEPS Action 2 hybrid rules. ICs may elect governance under the International Companies Act 1987 rather than the Companies Act 2006, and may elect to maintain accounts in any convertible currency, such as USD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992 (as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 60,000 (Samoa Tala) of annual taxable supplies made within Samoa; foreign and offshore-only licensors have no domestic registration nexus
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory electronic invoicing API, and no digital stamping regime is currently enforced by SRA. Tax invoices must contain the prescribed particulars under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992 (supplier name/TIN, recipient details, description, and VAGST amount). VAGST returns must be filed electronically through the SRA online portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods (physical removal from Samoa) and supplies of services to persons carrying on business outside Samoa, where the services are performed and exploited outside Samoa, are zero-rated under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992. For film licensing and royalty income, the licensing supply must be made to a non-resident licensee, the copyright exploitation must occur outside Samoa, and the IC must retain documentary proof; pure royalties and licensing fees to offshore distributors qualify as zero-rated export supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable to pure services: no Customs Export Declaration or Bill of Lading is required for a film-rights license; such documents would only be required if physical media is shipped out of Samoa
Fully executed film license or distribution agreement (ISIC 5911 scope) identifying licensee territory, titles, and royalty consideration
VAGST tax invoice or royalty statement referencing the zero-rated export supply
Bank SWIFT wire advice or inward remittance certificate evidencing payment from the offshore licensee
Certificate of Incorporation (International Company) and TIN (if registered)
Schedule of licensed territories and exploitation/usage report demonstrating offshore use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SRA may audit zero-rating claims and require the IC to substantiate the offshore supply. If substantiation fails, the supply is recharacterized as taxable at 15% VAGST with interest accruing from the original due date. The Tax Administration Act 2011 and the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992 provide for civil penalties, including up to 150% of the tax shortfall for willful evasion, retrospective clawbacks, and criminal liability for fraudulent claims, with fines up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 3 years for responsible officers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), acting through the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Exchange Control Regulations 1980, and the Financial Institutions Act 1996 (as amended); licensed authorized dealers execute CBS-approved foreign-currency transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is partially convertible: current-account flows such as royalties, licence fees, and trade settlements are freely processible through licensed authorized dealers, whereas resident capital-account transactions require CBS approval. A non-resident Samoan International Company operating entirely in foreign currency benefits from a statutory exchange-control ring-fence, so profit remittance, dividend payments, and capital repatriation are executable in USD/EUR without Tala conversion or CBS liquidity gating; only an intentional conversion into Tala triggers central-bank exchange-control filings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident exporters, Samoa requires export proceeds to be received through an authorized dealer and, where commercial operations require Tala, the foreign currency must be surrendered and converted to WST within thirty (30) days of receipt; no export proceeds are exempt without CBS approval. Non-resident International Companies in film copyright licensing are outside this surrender regime: 100% of film-distribution licence-fee receipts may be retained in designated foreign-currency accounts, and no mandatory conversion ratio is imposed on IC treasury operations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign-currency Operational Account (USD/EUR) with separate Capital Escrow Account available
Multi-currency Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account with SWIFT and trade-finance desk
USD/AUD Operational Account with commercial letters of credit and export settlement infrastructure

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — Samoa has no digital EMI or electronic-money-institution licensing framework, and the Financial Institutions Act 1996 prohibits unlicensed entities from taking deposits or providing payment services to Samoa-resident persons. Offshore EMIs cannot serve as a Samoan clearing rail for WST settlements and should be restricted to third-country USD/EUR receivables and payables outside the CBS perimeter; a licensed Samoan commercial bank remains mandatory as the primary account-and-liquidity spine.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted: no director is statutorily required to appear physically in Samoa. Samoan banks accept an apostilled corporate KYC pack, certified board resolutions, and a mandatory video-conference compliance interview with each director and the ultimate beneficial owner. A physical visit or appointment of the IC's licensed Samoan registered agent as a signatory materially shortens onboarding and reduces Enhanced Due Diligence referrals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore International Company classification and perceived absence of substance trigger mandatory Enhanced Due Diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) certificate of incorporation and good standing; International Companies Act 2012 tax-exemption certificate; licensed Samoa trust-company engagement letter; board minutes confirming Island-based administration; audited IC financial statements; and a substance statement demonstrating management, decision-making, and licence-agreement custody in Samoa.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty and licence-fee inflows from multiple foreign distributors without verifiable film-rights documentation are profiled as a value-laundering vector through intellectual property.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain-of-title legal opinion; executed acquisition/distribution agreements; sub-licence schedules; sales-agency statements; distributor invoices matched to inbound MT103 references; royalty-statement waterfall; and an independent auditor's funds-flow mapping from each licensee to the IC's Samoan account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lumpy inbound capital injections inconsistent with declared share capital and film-catalogue size trigger source-of-funds and source-of-wealth challenges.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder subscription resolution or shareholder-loan agreement; investor source-of-wealth statements; film-catalogue valuation or option-purchase agreements; remitter bank pedigree correspondence; and CBS-declared purpose coding under BPM6 as direct-investment equity or charges for the use of intellectual property.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital and licence prepayments must arrive via SWIFT MT103 quoting the IC's exact legal name, Samoan account number, and a narrative reference such as 'SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION' or 'FILM LICENCE PREPAYMENT' together with the underlying contract number. The receiving authorized dealer maps the credit to the CBS international-transactions reporting code for direct-investment equity or services royalties; all foreign-currency receipts post directly to the IC's non-resident account with zero conversion and no surrender obligation, and any deliberate Tala conversion requires a CBS exchange-control return.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Film-licensing outbound settlements run through SWIFT MT103 for producer advances, sales-agent commissions, and residuals, with reference to the underlying licensing invoice; large library acquisitions may be settled by irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit at sight or 30-90 days usance against delivery of master files, chain-of-title documents, and inspection certificates. MT202 COV is used for nostro-cleared interbank cover payments, and all messages are subject to currency- and counterparty-screening protocols consistent with Samoa's AML/CFT framework.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable foreign-exchange forwards on WST cross-pairs executed through licensed Samoan authorized dealers, subject to CBS conversion reporting where Tala settlement occurs
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST/USD placed offshore with OECD investment-grade counterparties to cap residual Tala exposure without Samoa liquidity commitment
Cross-currency swaps covering USD/EUR production and distribution cash-flow repricing, documented under ISDA/CSA terms and notified to the CBS where any leg converts to Tala
Vanilla FX options and foreign-currency interest-rate swaps for multi-picture production financing, permitted when maturity and notional align with documented film-licence cash flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Renewal Fee for International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour of Samoa (lodged through licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each anniversary of incorporation; a grace period of 30 days after the anniversary is available before late penalties attach
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment fee accrues at 10% per month or part month on the outstanding annual fee; continued default for up to 6 months enables the Registrar to initiate administrative strike-off of the International Company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return / Confirmation Statement of Company Details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour of Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to lodge the annual return triggers compounding late filing penalties and potential fines against directors; persistent non-lodgement for more than 6 months can lead to administrative strike-off and asset vesting in the Crown.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit threshold applies to a Samoa International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended). An audit is required only where the board or shareholders resolve to prepare audited financial statements, or where a financier or contractual counterparty imposes an audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or comparable internationally accepted accounting principles (e.g., US GAAP or UK GAAP); accounts need not be filed with the Registrar unless the company opts to do so.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, before the Annual Return deadline, the licensed registered agent must verify that the Register of Members accurately reflects all share transfers executed during the year and re-confirm the identity and ownership of each ultimate beneficial owner under Samoa Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing legislation. Share transfer instruments must be lodged with the registered agent within 14 days after transfer execution, and the Register of Members and UBO register must be updated before the annual confirmation is filed.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 per audit engagement, if voluntarily procured

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for International Companies (standard Samoa resident corporate rate is 27%; ICs are wholly exempt from Samoa income tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full exemption from Samoa corporate income tax, capital gains tax, and withholding taxes under the International Companies Act regime; no stamp duty on share transfers; the annual government fee replaces income tax liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Samoa income tax return (Form CIT) is filed by International Companies. The registered agent files the 'Annual Return for International Company' through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) e-filing portal or through a licensed SIFA registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Return due within 30 days of the anniversary of incorporation; annual government fee payable at the anniversary date in advance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name and registered company number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State exact International Company name as on the Certificate of Incorporation.
Must be the physical office of the registered agent; cannot be a PO Box.
Agent must be a licensed SIFA agent; consent must be signed by the agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors' full names, residential addresses, and passport numbers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident directors, list foreign address and indicate country; no Samoan tax number is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholders and issued share class details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the shareholder's name and address are entered; bearer shares must be eliminated before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the company has not conducted business in Samoa and is not subject to Samoa income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners should ensure the company has not derived Samoa-source income; if it has, full domestic tax registration is required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of annual return attracts a fixed penalty of WST 500; overdue annual government fee attracts a daily surcharge; continuing default after 60 days' notice leads to administrative strike-off and deemed dissolution, with asset escheatment to the Samoa Government.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for International Company dividends and deemed distributions; Samoa does not impose withholding tax on distributions made by an International Company to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No formal treaty relief step is needed for an International Company because its profits and distributions are exempt from Samoa tax. If a reduced treaty rate were sought for a hypothetically taxable payment, the beneficial owner must obtain a Samoa Tax Resident Certificate, secure a foreign tax residency certificate from the residence state, file the Samoa withholding tax relief application with the Ministry of Revenue / SIFA before payment, and provide certification of beneficial ownership. The payer must retain the approved relief notice and Tax Residency Certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: International Company payments of film royalties, license fees, or interest to non-residents are not subject to Samoa withholding tax because such payments have no Samoa source. If the payer were a resident Samoa company, the general non-resident statutory WHT rate is 15% for royalties and 15% for interest, with treaty rates potentially reduced to 0-10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: International Companies have no statutory Local File/Master File threshold because they are tax-exempt. Samoa's Income Tax Act 2012 arm's length rules apply to resident companies with cross-border related party transactions above WST 500,000 in annual aggregate turnover; a Master File is recommended when group turnover exceeds WST 50 million. In the IC context, SIFA's Economic Substance Form 1 requires annual disclosure of gross income from relevant activity and substance indicators in Samoa regardless of amount.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Samoa Economic Substance Regulations 2019 (as amended) apply to International Companies engaged in relevant activities. Independent film licensing is an 'IP business' / 'distribution and service centre' activity; the IC must be managed and controlled in Samoa, maintain a physical office and local employees, and make adequate local expenditures. A mere mailbox with no operational substance in Samoa is prohibited and can lead to enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a false declaration that the international company conducted no Samoa business while servicing or licensing film distribution to Samoan customers or collecting Samoa-source revenues.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company is re-characterized as a resident taxable entity; back taxes assessed at the 27% corporate rate with a 100% shortfall penalty and daily late-payment interest. Criminal fine up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for willful evasion under the Income Tax Act 2012.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute false declarations assume personal liability for the unpaid tax; courts may pierce the corporate veil and issue freezes and travel bans, and may impose custodial sentences in addition to civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Owning film copyrights and licensing income through a letterbox Samoa IC with no office, employees, or management in Samoa, and no economic substance declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Economic Substance Regulations 2019, SIFA can impose penalties up to WST 250,000 plus WST 1,000 per day, compel production of board minutes and bank records, and notify the tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and registered agents may be de-registered, individually fined, and prohibited from acting as agents or forming companies for up to 5 years; they may also be ordered to compensate authorities for enforcement costs.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using nominees, undisclosed beneficiaries, bearer instruments, or shell layers while paying film royalties through Swift wires without AML/KYC declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of Samoa Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism legislation carries fines up to WST 200,000 for the company and imprisonment up to 7 years for responsible officers; funds and bank accounts can be frozen and forfeited.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable for directing or allowing the transaction; personal forfeiture orders, travel bans, extradition agreements, and custodial penalties apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Statements to the Registrar of International Companies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting an annual return or economic substance declaration containing false registered agent consent, false director/shareholder identifiers, or fictitious declared substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies Act, false statements constitute an offense carrying a fine not exceeding WST 50,000 and imprisonment up to 4 years; the Registrar's rectification order and striking-off may follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing is available for fraud: directors must make restitution for all proceeds received, reimburse SIFA costs, and may be subject to disqualification and removal from Samoa.
